subject_group: 6.2.10 Vehicle control function air data safety

versions.text: Criterion: Verify safe integration of air data sensors with VCF. Standard: The VCF air data architecture provides control scheduling/inputs for all tasks throughout the flight envelope and provides sufficient processing, memory, and data communications capability to meet the requirements for the VCF integrated functions (e.g., navigation, engines, displays, and Stores Management System (SMS)), both internal and external to the VCF. Air data parameters from any single source or combination of sources are transmitted only after verification of accuracy. The air data function supports: a. Pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight built-in-test (BIT). b. Redundancy and fault tolerance – Fail-operational/fail-operational/fail-safe capability. Method of Compliance: Verification methods for control functionality and performance of the integration of the air data with the VCF include analysis, test (FMET (failure modes and effects testing), ground and flight), simulation, demonstration and review of documentation. Verification methods for air data communication include Hardware-In-The Loop (HITL) tests such as FMET. References: JSSG-2008: 3.0, 3.1, 3.1.2.1, 3.1.7, 3.1.7.2, 3.1.7.3, 3.1.11, 3.1.13.4, 3.1.17, 3.2.2.2.12, 3.2.2.4, 3.2.2.5.2, associated section 4 paragraphs. 14 CFR 23.141-23.253, 25.21-25.255, 23.321-23.459, 25.321-25.459, 23.1501- 23.1529, 25.1501-25.1529.

Standard: The VCF air data architecture provides control scheduling and valid inputs for all tasks throughout the RORH and provides processing, memory, and data communications capability to meet the requirements for the VCF integrated functions (e.g., navigation, engines, displays, and SMS), both internal and external to the VCF. In order to provide valid inputs, the air data function supports: a. Fault detection of the system pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight. b. Redundancy and fault tolerance: fail-operational/fail-safe capability. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review design documents to verify redundancy management is implemented within requirements. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct analysis of air data processing and transmission needs of the integrated system to confirm the VCF architecture meets the needs of functions that rely on air data.
  (2) Complete fault tree and FMECA to identify failure modes, failure rates, and consequences. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct FMET with VCF HITL to verify fault detection, system redundancy, and fault tolerance.
    (2) Lab test: Verify that outputs of the air data system for the nominal case as well as in the presence of air data failures are expected values and are transmitted for use throughout the air vehicle. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
      (1) Conduct flight test operations to verify that the air data system operates in-flight as designed.
